correctness.rationale: All hypotheses used in the counterexample were reconstructed from the estimator definition. IID exponential observations are α-mixing; the Gaussian kernel and \(b_n=n^{-1/2}\) satisfy the displayed kernel/bandwidth conditions; and \(\beta=1/2\) is allowed. Exact Gaussian integration gives the deterministic tail benchmark, continuity yields a positive-probability neighborhood with nonzero limiting error, and that nonzero limit forces an infinite Lebesgue-time squared-error integral. No finite computation or asymptotic numerical experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The finding invalidates a recent global consistency theorem on its stated infinite time domain using a canonical IID exponential model and Gaussian kernel. The failure is structural rather than a tiny numerical exception: a sample-dependent tail level produces infinite integrated risk for every sample size. This isolates the missing finite-domain or integrable-weight requirement while preserving the possibility of valid fixed-time or compact-domain results.
